chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, and Hisham ibn al-Hakam, and Durust ibn Abi Mansur, from 'Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It was revealed regarding the kinship of the Progeny of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family), and it may also apply to your relatives.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Therefore, do not be among those who say for a thing that it is in one (and the same) thing.'
ai.seo_question: What does the verse 'Those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined' refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the command to 'join what Allah has commanded to be joined' primarily emphasizes maintaining kinship ties with the Prophet’s family (Ahl al-Bayt), while also encompassing one's own relatives. He adds a crucial theological nuance, cautioning against conflating the specific, elevated obligation towards the Ahl al-Bayt with the general obligation towards other relatives, thereby distinguishing their unique status in Shia jurisprudence and theology.
